title: Best Landing Page Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a landing page designer: what the package should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: A landing page has one job: turn visitors from an ad, email or post into buyers, sign-ups or bookings. Pages usually fail because they try to say everything, load slowly on phones, or were never connected to tracking. This guide helps you order a page built around a single goal.

faq.q: What is the difference between a landing page and a website?
faq.a: A website has many pages and many purposes. A landing page is a single page with one goal and usually one button, made for a specific campaign or offer. Many businesses have one website and several landing pages.

faq.q: Which tool will the page be built in?
faq.a: Landing pages are often built in a page builder, in WordPress, in Shopify, or in the landing page feature of an email or ad tool. Agree on the tool before ordering, and make sure you can edit text yourself afterwards.

faq.q: Do I need to write the text myself?
faq.a: Check the package. Some designers only design and build; others include copywriting. The words decide most of the result, so if you write them yourself, keep them short and focused on what the visitor gets.

faq.q: How do I know if the page works?
faq.a: Track the action that matters, such as a purchase, sign-up or booking, and compare it with the number of visitors. Ask for tracking to be set up and tested before you send traffic to the page.

faq.q: Should I ask for two versions to test?
faq.a: If you plan to spend on ads, yes. Two versions of the headline or the top section let you learn what visitors respond to. Many designers offer a second variant as an add-on.
